title: Widest Pair of Indices With Equal Range Sum
summary: Given two binary arrays, find the widest pair of indices where the sum of elements from i to j in the first array equals the sum of elements from i to j in the second array.
statement: Given two binary arrays, find the widest pair of indices where the sum of elements from i to j in the first array equals the sum of elements from i to j in the second array. The widest pair is defined by the maximum distance between i and j. Return this distance; otherwise, return 0.
constraints: The two lists have equal length from 1 through 100000 and contain nonnegative integers.
A range qualifies when its sum in nums1 equals its sum at the same indices in nums2.
Return the maximum qualifying range length, or zero when none exists.
hints: Equal range sums mean the prefix difference has the same value at both range boundaries.
Track the earliest index for each cumulative nums1-minus-nums2 difference.
Seed difference zero at -1; on repeats maximize current index minus earliest index.
Subtracting equal prefix differences cancels everything outside the range, and retaining the earliest index gives the widest range for each endpoint.
editorial: Subtracting equal prefix differences cancels everything outside the range, and retaining the earliest index gives the widest range for each endpoint.

tests.explanation: The range from index zero through two has equal sums, giving width three.
Only the second position has equal values, so the widest range has length one.
